name: Auto-Select
summary: A framework that switches between selection techniques in real time: each technique reports how suitable it is for the current scene density and object speed, and the best-suited one is used at that moment.
howItWorks: Each technique implements a suitability index computed every frame from scene attributes such as the number of nearby objects and cursor velocity; an analyser picks the highest one. The prototype combined Bendcast (suited to sparse, slow scenes) and Expand (suited to dense, fast ones), on a 50-inch HDTV with a PlayStation Move controller. In the study, Auto-Select was significantly faster than Expand but slower than Bendcast; the authors judged the approach promising but noted that switching can introduce drawbacks.
advantages: Combines the strengths of techniques suited to different conditions.
Extensible to any technique that can report a suitability score.
limitations: Switching techniques mid-task can confuse users.
Slower than Bendcast in the tested scenes.

relationships.note: Its other component is Bendcast, a bending-ray technique.
Also adapts the selection technique to context.

review.notes: Coded from the 3DUI 2013 full text. Environment coded desktop to match the vault's Expand entry (large TV, tracked controller). Bendcast is not a separate vault entry; related to Bent Pick Ray.
